# Tapir commands: Navigator Commands

The 92 commands of this group, with their parameters, results and examples. Every group and how a command is sent: [commands.md](https://archicad-api.com/commands.md).

## Navigator Commands

### PublishPublisherSet

Performs a publish operation on the currently opened project. Only the given publisher set will be published. The command answers when Archicad's API reports the publishing done; for a local or LAN output folder the answer names the folder and lists the files created or changed in it (writtenFiles). A large set can take minutes, so give the call a long enough timeout. The output format of each item is the one set in the publisher set: Archicad's API cannot choose it per call.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 0.1.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#PublishPublisherSet

Parameters:

- `publisherSetName` (string, required): The name of the publisher set.
- `outputPath` (string): Full local or LAN path for publishing. Optional, by default the path set in the settings of the publisher set will be used.
- `selectedNavigatorItemIds` (NavigatorItemIds): Optional publisher-tree navigator items to publish instead of the whole publisher set. Each item wraps its id in navigatorItemId, as the items of GetNavigatorItemTree do: [{"navigatorItemId": {"guid": "6E1C3A9B-0F2D-4B8E-9C7A-1D2E3F405162"}}], not [{"guid": "..."}].

Returns:

- `outputFolder` (string): The local or LAN folder the set was published to: outputPath, else the path saved in the publisher set. Absent when the set publishes elsewhere (to the Internet or a BIMcloud/Teamwork file server).
- `writtenFiles` (array of string): Full paths of the files in outputFolder and its subfolders that were created or changed while the command ran, as found when Archicad reported the publishing finished. Absent when outputFolder is absent or holds more than 20000 files and folders.

Grasshopper: `PublishPublisherSetComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/PublishPublisherSet.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/PublishPublisherSet.py): Publishes the first publisher set of the project with PublishPublisherSet. Needs at least one publisher set. The output goes to a new temporary folder instead of the path saved in the publisher set; the answer lists the files written there (writtenFiles). Publishing a large set takes long, so the call is given a generous timeout (in seconds).

### GetPublisherSets

Returns the publisher sets of the project with their saved output: the local or LAN path, the Teamwork file server path, or the Internet host and directory name.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetPublisherSets

Parameters: none.

Returns:

- `publisherSets` (array of object, required): The publisher sets of the project, in the order of the Publisher Sets map.
  - `name` (string, required): The name of the publisher set.
  - `rootNavigatorItemId` (NavigatorItemId, required): The navigator item ID of the root of the publisher set.
  - `path` (string): The saved local or LAN output path, when the set is published to files. When it is also uploaded to a Teamwork file server, this is the temporary local path.
  - `twFileServerPath` (string): The saved output path on the Teamwork file server, when the set is published to files onto a file server.
  - `host` (string): The saved host name, when the set is published to the Internet.
  - `dirName` (string): The saved directory name on the host, when the set is published to the Internet.

Grasshopper: `GetPublisherSetsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/GetPublisherSets.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/GetPublisherSets.py): Lists the publisher sets of the project and where each one publishes to, with GetPublisherSets.

### Create3DDocuments

Creates 3D Documents with the given names and reference IDs, in the Project Map's 3D Documents folder. Archicad gives each its starting settings; Get3DDocumentSettings reads them and Set3DDocumentSettings changes its view, cut and filter. Returns the databaseId and the Project Map navigatorItemId of each new 3D Document.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.1. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#Create3DDocuments

Parameters:

- `documentsData` (array of object, required): One item per new 3D Document.
  - `name` (string, required): The name of the new 3D Document.
  - `referenceId` (string, required): The reference ID of the new 3D Document.

Returns:

- `databases` (array of CreatedDatabase or ErrorItem, required): One item per input item, in the same order.

### CreateDetailMarkers

Places Detail markers with their clip polygon in the current floor plan, section or elevation, each with a new Detail viewpoint, like the Detail tool. GetDetailsOfElements reads them back.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateDetailMarkers

Parameters:

- `detailMarkersData` (array of object, required)
  - `clipPolygon` (array of Coordinate2D, required): The boundary of the cut out area, at least 3 points, without repeating the first one.
  - `polygonArcs` (array of PolyArc): Optional arcs of the boundary, with indices into clipPolygon.
  - `markerCoordinate` (Coordinate2D): Where the marker symbol is placed. Default is the first point of clipPolygon.
  - `angle` (number): Rotation of the marker symbol in radians. Default is that of the tool defaults.
  - `name` (string): Name of the new viewpoint. Default is that of the tool defaults.
  - `id` (string): Reference ID shown in the marker and in the Project Map. A '/' splits it between the two lines of the marker. Default is that of the tool defaults.
  - `floorIndex` (integer): Story of the marker when it is placed on a floor plan. Default is the current story.
  - `constructionElementsOnly` (boolean): Copy construction elements only: whether only the construction elements of the cut out area are copied into the new viewpoint (API_DetailType::constructionElementsOnly). Default is that of the tool defaults.

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `CreateDetailMarkersComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/CreateDetailMarkers.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/CreateDetailMarkers.py): Places a Detail marker on the current floor plan story with CreateDetailMarkers, then deletes it again. The marker cuts out a 4 x 3 m rectangle; Archicad creates a new Detail viewpoint for it, which is deleted together with the marker.

### ModifyDetailMarkers

Changes the name, the reference ID, the clip polygon, the boundary's pen and line type, the marker symbol's angle, always-horizontal setting and pen, and 'Copy construction elements only' of Detail and Worksheet markers. Not written: the base point (Archicad places it at the center of the clip polygon's bounding box when the marker is created), the viewpoint the marker refers to, and the marker symbol's other settings, which are parameters of the library part placed as the marker (markerId in GetDetailsOfElements). A value Archicad did not apply gets a failed execution result.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ModifyDetailMarkers

Parameters:

- `detailMarkersWithDetails` (array of object, required)
  - `elementId` (ElementId, required): A Detail or a Worksheet marker.
  - `name` (string): The new name of the viewpoint.
  - `id` (string): The new reference ID, shown in the marker and in the Project Map. A '/' splits it between the two lines of the marker.
  - `clipPolygon` (array of Coordinate2D): The new boundary of the cut out area, at least 3 points, without repeating the first one.
  - `polygonArcs` (array of PolyArc): Optional arcs of the new boundary, with indices into clipPolygon.
  - `penIndex` (integer): The new pen of the boundary (API_DetailType::pen).
  - `lineTypeIndex` (integer): Attribute index of the new line type of the boundary (API_DetailType::ltypeInd).
  - `angle` (number): The new rotation of the marker symbol, in radians (API_DetailType::angle).
  - `isHorizontalMarker` (boolean): Whether the marker symbol is always horizontal (API_DetailType::horizontalMarker).
  - `constructionElementsOnly` (boolean): Copy construction elements only (API_DetailType::constructionElementsOnly), as GetDetailsOfElements returns it.
  - `markerPenIndex` (integer): The new pen of the marker symbol, the library part placed as the marker (its markerId in GetDetailsOfElements).

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `ModifyDetailMarkersComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/ModifyDetailMarkers.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/ModifyDetailMarkers.py): Changes the ID, name, clip polygon, pens and angle of a Detail marker with ModifyDetailMarkers, reads them back, then deletes it. The script places its own Detail marker on the current floor plan story first (CreateDetailMarkers). ModifyDetailMarkers works on Worksheet markers the same way. penIndex and lineTypeIndex are the boundary's pen and line type, markerPenIndex the pen of the marker symbol; angle turns the marker symbol unless isHorizontalMarker keeps it horizontal. constructionElementsOnly is the marker's 'Copy construction elements only' setting.

### CreateLayout

Creates Layouts and their backing master layouts. Archicad inserts a new layout at the first place of its subset, renumbering the sheets after it; previousNavigatorItemId or position 'last' places it after an existing sheet or at the end instead. A custom layout number does not leave the layout out of the numbering; layoutParameters.doNotIncludeInNumbering does. A layout that was created but could not be placed is returned with both its databaseId and the error.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 1.4.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateLayout

Parameters:

- `layoutsData` (array of object, required)
  - `masterLayoutName` (string)
  - `masterNavigatorItemId` (NavigatorItemId)
  - `layoutName` (string, required)
  - `parentNavigatorItemId` (NavigatorItemId)
  - `previousNavigatorItemId` (NavigatorItemId): The sibling after which the new layout is placed, as in MoveNavigatorItem. It must be a child of parentNavigatorItemId (or of the Layout Book root when that is omitted). Cannot be combined with position.
  - `position` (LayoutInsertionPosition): Archicad inserts new layouts at the first place, which renumbers the sheets after them; "last" appends it after the existing children instead. Cannot be combined with previousNavigatorItemId.
  - `paperWidth` (number): Optional paper width in mm, used together with paperHeight. Sets the size of the new layout, and of the master layout when this command creates it from masterLayoutName: a new master starts with the template's default size, which layoutParameters cannot change. An existing master keeps its size. Wins over layoutParameters.horizontalSize.
  - `paperHeight` (number): Optional paper height in mm, used together with paperWidth. See paperWidth. Wins over layoutParameters.verticalSize.
  - `layoutParameters` (object)

Returns:

- `databases` (array of DatabaseIdArrayItem or ErrorItem or object, required)

Grasshopper: `CreateLayoutComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/CreateLayout.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/CreateLayout.py): Creates a layout at the end of the Layout Book with CreateLayout, then deletes it again. Needs at least one master layout.

### ChangeLayoutSubsetSettings

Changes the settings of existing Layout Book subsets (name, ID prefix, numbering style, start at, ...), the fields of CreateLayoutSubset; the ones not given keep their value. The Archicad API can neither change the settings of a subset nor delete one, so a new subset is created with the changed settings right after the old one, and the old one's layouts and subsets are moved into it in their order; when a move fails, the ones moved before are moved back. The old subset is left empty, and its id is returned with the new one's: delete it in Archicad. These navigator functions are not undoable.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.1. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ChangeLayoutSubsetSettings

Parameters:

- `subsets` (array of object, required): The Layout Book subsets to change, each with the settings to change.
  - `navigatorItemId` (NavigatorItemId, required): The subset to change, from GetNavigatorItemTree or CreateLayoutSubset.
  - `settings` (LayoutSubsetSettingsData, required): The settings to change. The ones not given keep the value the subset has.

Returns:

- `subsets` (array of object or ErrorItem, required): One item per input subset, in the same order: the subset that now has the settings and the layouts, and the old subset, left empty, or an error.

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/ChangeLayoutSubsetSettings.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/ChangeLayoutSubsetSettings.py): Changes the ID prefix and numbering of a Layout Book subset with ChangeLayoutSubsetSettings. Creates a subset with one layout first. The command moves the layout into a new subset with the new settings and leaves the old subset empty; the layout and its master are deleted at the end, the two subsets stay in the Layout Book: subsets cannot be deleted through the Archicad API.

### CreateDrawings

Creates Drawing elements on the specified or active layout from navigator items.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 1.4.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateDrawings

Parameters:

- `drawingsData` (array of object, required)
  - `navigatorItemId` (NavigatorItemId, required)
  - `layoutDatabaseId` (DatabaseId)
  - `name` (string): Custom title name of the new Drawing. Giving a name implies nameType CustomName unless nameType is set explicitly.
  - `nameType` (DrawingNameType): Defaults to CustomName when name is given, otherwise to the Drawing tool's current default.
  - `position` (Coordinate2D, required): Where the Drawing is placed on the layout, in meters; this becomes its pos. Without clipPolygon it is the lower left corner of the Drawing (before rotation). With clipPolygon it is the point where the origin of the source view lands (on a floor plan the project origin), also when the source view stores its zoom: a model point (x, y) appears at position + scale * drawing scale * (x, y), rotated by angle, and the clipPolygon chooses which part is shown.
  - `scale` (number): Scale ratio applied to the drawing relative to its source view (API_DrawingType::ratio). Defaults to 1.0.
  - `angle` (number): Rotation angle of the drawing in radians. Defaults to the Drawing tool's current default.
  - `drawingScale` (number): Ignored: Archicad takes the scale from the source view (API_DrawingType::drawingScale is output only). GetDetailsOfElements returns the scale the Drawing got.
  - `modelOffset` (Coordinate2D): Offset of the model origin within the drawing, in model meters. Archicad uses it only with clipPolygon and then adds modelOffset * drawing scale (times scale, rotated by angle) to the new Drawing's pos; without clipPolygon it is ignored. Defaults to the Drawing tool's current default.
  - `anchorPoint` (DrawingAnchorPoint): The node of the drawing's bounding box the drawing is placed by. Used only when useOwnOriginAsAnchor is false; giving anchorPoint makes useOwnOriginAsAnchor default to false. Defaults to Center.
  - `useOwnOriginAsAnchor` (boolean): Whether the drawing is placed by its own origin instead of anchorPoint. Defaults to false when anchorPoint is given, otherwise to the Drawing tool's current default.
  - `clipPolygon` (array of Coordinate2D): Optional polygon to clip the drawing with, in layout coordinates (meters on the layout, the same coordinate system as position) - not the coordinates of the source view's model. Stored as given: position, angle, scale and modelOffset are not applied to it, and it does not move the content (see position).

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `CreateDrawingsComponent`, `DrawingsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/CreateDrawings.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/CreateDrawings.py): Places the first story of the project as a Drawing on the first layout with CreateDrawings. Needs at least one layout. Deletes the new Drawing at the end.

### ChangeDrawingLink

Relinks a Drawing to a different source navigator item. Archicad has no in-place relink API, so this recreates the Drawing against the new source and deletes the original - the returned elementId is a NEW guid, not the input one. The Drawing Title marker's own position is not preserved (undocumented Archicad limitation). The new source view is made current before the Drawing is created (Archicad 27 or later), and the window and story that were active when the command started are restored afterwards; the view settings (zoom, layers, scale) shown in that window are not restored.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.7. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ChangeDrawingLink

Parameters:

- `drawingsWithNewLinks` (array of object, required)
  - `elementId` (ElementId, required)
  - `navigatorItemId` (NavigatorItemId, required)
  - `layoutDatabaseId` (DatabaseId, required)

Returns:

- `elements` (array of ElementIdOrError, required): One result per input item. On success, elementId is the NEW Drawing's identifier - relinking necessarily replaces the element, it cannot keep the original guid.

Grasshopper: `ChangeDrawingLinkComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/ChangeDrawingLink.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/ChangeDrawingLink.py): Places a Drawing of the first story on a layout, then links it to the second story with ChangeDrawingLink. Needs at least two stories and a layout. ChangeDrawingLink recreates the Drawing, so it returns a new element id. Deletes the Drawing at the end.

  - `masterLayoutName` (string): The name of the master layout of the layout. Not present for master layouts.
  - `customData` (array of LayoutCustomData)

Grasshopper: `GetLayoutSettingsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/GetLayoutSettings.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/GetLayoutSettings.py): Prints the size, margins, numbering, master layout and custom data of every layout with GetLayoutSettings.

### SetLayoutSettings

Sets settings of layouts, including their master layout and Layout Info Panel custom data fields. In Teamwork the layout settings must be reserved first in Archicad (Layout Book > Reserve Layout Settings); the Archicad API cannot reserve them, and ReserveElements does not. GetTeamworkOwnersOfDatabases shows who holds a layout.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 1.1.7. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SetLayoutSettings

Parameters:

- `layoutsData` (array of object, required)
  - `layoutDatabaseId` (DatabaseId)
  - `layoutNavigatorItemId` (NavigatorItemId)
  - `layoutName` (string): The new name of the layout or master layout (its database name, as returned by GetDatabases and GetLayoutSettings). A custom name of its Navigator item is changed with RenameNavigatorItem instead.
  - `horizontalSize` (number)
  - `verticalSize` (number)
  - `leftMargin` (number)
  - `topMargin` (number)
  - `rightMargin` (number)
  - `bottomMargin` (number)
  - `customLayoutNumber` (string)
  - `customLayoutNumbering` (boolean)
  - `doNotIncludeInNumbering` (boolean)
  - `showMasterBelow` (boolean)
  - `masterNavigatorItemId` (NavigatorItemId): The master layout to assign to the layout, as its Layout Book navigator item. Only layouts can be given a master layout, master layouts cannot.
  - `masterLayoutDatabaseId` (DatabaseId): The master layout to assign to the layout, as its database. Used when masterNavigatorItemId is not given.
  - `masterLayoutName` (string): The master layout to assign to the layout, by name. Used when neither masterNavigatorItemId nor masterLayoutDatabaseId is given.
  - `customData` (array of LayoutCustomDataToSet)

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `SetLayoutSettingsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/SetLayoutSettings.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/SetLayoutSettings.py): Renames the first layout with SetLayoutSettings, reads it back, then restores the original name. Needs at least one layout.

### GetModelViewOptionDetails

Gets the settings stored in model view option combinations (Document > Model View > Model View Options), all of them or the ones given by id or by name: the model view options in the fields of GetViewOptions, and the options library parts add to the combination (gdlOptions) with their GDL parameter values. Read-only: the Archicad API has no function to change, rename or create a stored combination; SetViewOptions changes the options of the current window. Available from Archicad 27.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetModelViewOptionDetails

Parameters:

  - `modelViewOptionId` (object): The identifier of the model view option combination (see FindModelViewOption).
  - `name` (string): The name of the model view option combination, as shown in Document > Model View > Model View Options.

Returns:

Requires Archicad 27 or later.

### GetViewOptions

Gets the model view options and on-screen view options of the current plan window, and the index and name of the model view option combination it applies.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetViewOptions

Parameters: none.

Returns:

- `modelViewOptionIndex` (integer, required): The index of the model view option combination the window applies, 0 when its options are not a stored combination (Custom). It is the index FindModelViewOption and GetModelViewOptionDetails return, which is not always the position in the list of GetModelViewOptions.
- `modelViewOptionName` (string, required): The name of that combination, empty when there is none. Archicad may renumber the combinations when the view options of a window change, so look the index up by this name (FindModelViewOption) before switching back to it with SetViewOptions.
- `viewOptions` (ViewOptions, required)

Grasshopper: `GetViewOptionsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/GetViewOptions.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/GetViewOptions.py): Prints the model view options and on-screen view options of the current plan window with GetViewOptions.

### SetViewOptions

Switches the current plan window to a model view option combination by index, and/or changes the given model view options and on-screen view options. With an index, the model view options stored in the combination apply. The options are read back, and a given field Archicad did not keep (with an index, a given on-screen view option) fails the call with the value it kept; the fields Archicad kept stay changed. Archicad 29 does not keep the railing components shown in the floor plan (modelViewOptions.railing, railing2DDisplayComp*) changed this way, so such a change is reported as not kept; GetViewOptions reads them.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SetViewOptions

Parameters:

- `modelViewOptionIndex` (integer): Switches the window to the model view option combination with this index, as GetViewOptions, FindModelViewOption and GetModelViewOptionDetails return it. Archicad then applies the model view options stored in the combination: viewOptions.modelViewOptions are not applied together with an index, viewOptions.onScreenViewOptions are. Archicad may renumber the combinations when the view options of a window change, so look the index up by name with FindModelViewOption right before switching.
- `viewOptions` (ViewOptionsUpdate)


Grasshopper: `SetViewOptionsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/SetViewOptions.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/SetViewOptions.py): Switches the fill handles of the current plan window with SetViewOptions, then restores the original options. Run it with a floor plan, section or elevation window in front.

### Set3DCutPlanes

Sets the 3D cut planes (pa*x + pb*y + pc*z = pd, cutting away the side the normal points to), with the pen and surface of their cut faces, and turns 3D Cutaway on. An empty cutPlanes array switches the 3D cut off.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 1.3.1. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#Set3DCutPlanes

Parameters:

- `cutPlanes` (array of CutPlane, required): The cut planes, replacing the current ones. Each cuts away the side of its plane that its normal vector (pa, pb, pc) points to; several planes cut away the union of those sides. Setting planes also turns 3D Cutaway on (off and on again when it is on), which puts them in force in the 3D window. An empty array switches the 3D cut off. A plane without cutPen or cutSurfaceId keeps those of the current plane in its place, or of the last current plane; where there is none, or it is pen 0 or no surface (which draws black), it takes customPen and customSurfaceId.
- `useCustom` (boolean): The Custom setting of the cut faces, kept for the 3D Cutting Planes settings; in the Archicad 29 3D window the cut faces take each plane's cutSurfaceId either way. Left unchanged when omitted.
- `customPen` (integer): The pen of the cut edges when useCustom is true. Left unchanged when omitted.
- `customSurfaceId` (AttributeId): The surface of the cut faces when useCustom is true. Left unchanged when omitted.


Grasshopper: `Set3DCutPlanesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/Set3DCutPlanes.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/Set3DCutPlanes.py): Sets one 3D cut plane with Set3DCutPlanes, then restores the original 3D cut. An empty cutPlanes array switches the 3D cut off.

### Get3DCutPlanes

Gets whether the 3D cut planes are on, the cut planes (pa, pb, pc, pd) of the 3D window with the pen and surface of their cut faces, and the custom cut pen and surface, in the form accepted by Set3DCutPlanes.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.3. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#Get3DCutPlanes

Parameters: none.

Returns:

- `isCutPlanes` (boolean, required): Whether the 3D cut planes are switched on.
- `useCustom` (boolean, required): Whether the cut faces of the elements take customPen and customSurfaceId.
- `customPen` (integer): The pen of the cut edges when useCustom is true. Missing when it is no valid pen (0).
- `customSurfaceId` (AttributeId): The surface of the cut faces when useCustom is true. Missing when it is no surface attribute.
- `cutPlanes` (array of CutPlane, required): The cut planes, in the form accepted by Set3DCutPlanes: pa*x + pb*y + pc*z = pd, pd in meters.

Grasshopper: `Get3DCutPlanesComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/Get3DCutPlanes.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/Get3DCutPlanes.py): Prints whether the 3D cut is on and the cut planes of the 3D window with Get3DCutPlanes.

### Get3DProjectionSettings

Gets the 3D projection settings of the 3D window: whether it is perspective or axonometric, the camera and target position, view cone, roll angle, distance and azimuth of a perspective, or the projection type, azimuth and transformation matrix of an axonometry, and the sun position of either (date and time or azimuth and altitude).

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.2. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#Get3DProjectionSettings

Parameters: none.

Returns:

- `isPersp` (boolean, required): True for a perspective projection, false for an axonometric one.
- `cameraElementId` (ElementId): The Camera element the projection was set from. Missing when the projection does not come from a camera.
- `activeCameraSetElementId` (ElementId): The active Camera Set element. Missing when there is none.
- `perspective` (PerspectiveProjectionParameters): The perspective parameters. Present only when isPersp is true.
- `axonometric` (object): The parameters of an axonometric projection. Present only when isPersp is false.
  - `projectionType` (AxonometryProjectionType, required)
  - `azimuth` (number, required): The camera azimuth in degrees, the Azimuth of the 3D Projection Settings dialog: for a side view the direction from the model to the camera, counterclockwise from the X axis (270 looks from the south). A predefined axonometry looks from 45 degrees further on.
  - `transformationMatrix` (array of number, required): The 3x4 transformation matrix of the axonometric projection, row by row (12 numbers).
  - `sun` (ProjectionSunSettings, required): The sun position of the axonometry.

Grasshopper: `Get3DProjectionSettingsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/Get3DProjectionSettings.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/Get3DProjectionSettings.py): Prints the perspective camera or the axonometric projection of the 3D window with Get3DProjectionSettings.

### Set3DProjectionSettings

Sets a perspective or an axonometric projection for the 3D window. Every perspective parameter but sun is required: read a known good set with Get3DProjectionSettings and pass it back, with the values to change replaced. An axonometry changes only the values given: the projection type, the azimuth, the transformation matrix and the sun. The sun of either changes only the values given in it and is kept when sun is missing. The 3D window shows the change after a rebuild (RebuildView), e.g. before SaveCurrentWindowAsImage.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 1.7.2. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#Set3DProjectionSettings

Parameters:

- `perspective` (PerspectiveProjectionParameters)
- `axonometry` (object): Makes the projection axonometric. Only the given values change, in sun too; the others are kept from the current axonometry, or from the last one when the projection is a perspective.
  - `projectionType` (AxonometryProjectionType)
  - `azimuth` (number): The camera azimuth in degrees, the Azimuth of the 3D Projection Settings dialog: for a side view the direction from the model to the camera, counterclockwise from the X axis (270 looks from the south). A predefined axonometry looks from 45 degrees further on.
  - `transformationMatrix` (array of number): The 3x4 transformation matrix of the axonometric projection, row by row (12 numbers), as Get3DProjectionSettings returns it. Its 3x3 part must be invertible.
  - `sun` (ProjectionSunSettings): The sun position of the axonometry. Only the values given change.


Grasshopper: `Set3DProjectionSettingsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/Set3DProjectionSettings.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/Set3DProjectionSettings.py): Raises the camera of the 3D perspective by 1 m and puts its sun at 21 June 13:30, or turns the axonometry to isometric, with Set3DProjectionSettings. The sun of a projection only changes the values given in sun; the others are kept. Restores the original projection at the end.

### GetCameras

Gets the Camera Sets (camera paths) of the project with their name, whether the set is the active one, its current camera, and its cameras in path order. Each camera has its element id, whether it is active in the path, its pen, and its perspective: camera and target position, distance, azimuth, view cone, roll angle, two-point perspective and sun, in the shape Set3DProjectionSettings accepts, so passing a camera's perspective there shows its view in the 3D window. Archicad cameras are always perspective; they have no name of their own.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetCameras

Parameters: none.

Returns:

- `cameraSets` (array of object, required): The Camera Sets (camera paths) of the project, each with its cameras.
  - `cameraSetElementId` (ElementId, required)
  - `name` (string, required): The name of the Camera Set, as the navigator shows it.
  - `isActive` (boolean, required): True for the active Camera Set.
  - `activeCameraElementId` (ElementId): The current camera of the set. Missing when the set has none.
  - `cameras` (array of object, required): The cameras of the set, in the order of the path.

Grasshopper: `GetCamerasComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/GetCameras.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/GetCameras.py): Prints the Camera Sets of the project with their cameras with GetCameras, then shows the first camera's view in the 3D window with Set3DProjectionSettings.

### CreateCameraSets

Creates empty Camera Sets (camera paths) with the given names, and makes one the active Camera Set when isActive is true. Returns their element ids, which GetCameras lists as cameraSetElementId. Delete them with DeleteElements.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.1. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateCameraSets

Parameters:

- `cameraSets` (array of object, required): The Camera Sets (camera paths) to create, each empty: cameras are added to them later.
  - `name` (string, required): The name of the new Camera Set, as the navigator shows it.
  - `isActive` (boolean): If true, the new set becomes the active Camera Set, and the one active before is no longer active. Default is false.

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required): The element ids of the new Camera Sets, in the order of the input, or an error for each one that could not be created. GetCameras lists them as cameraSetElementId.

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/CreateCameraSets.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/CreateCameraSets.py): Creates an empty Camera Set (camera path) named "Viewpoints" with CreateCameraSets, makes it the active set, and lists the Camera Sets with GetCameras.

### ModifyCameraSets

Renames Camera Sets (camera paths) and makes one of them the active Camera Set (isActive true); the set active before is then no longer active. Values not given are kept.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.1. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ModifyCameraSets

Parameters:

- `cameraSets` (array of object, required): The Camera Sets to change, each with the values to change; the values not given are kept.
  - `cameraSetElementId` (ElementId, required): The Camera Set, as GetCameras or CreateCameraSets returns it.
  - `name` (string): The new name of the Camera Set, as the navigator shows it.
  - `isActive` (boolean): true makes the set the active Camera Set, and the one active before is no longer active. false is refused: one set is always the active one, so make another set active instead.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required): One result for each Camera Set of the input, in its order.

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/ModifyCameraSets.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/ModifyCameraSets.py): Renames the first Camera Set GetCameras lists to "Renderer views" and makes it the active Camera Set with ModifyCameraSets.

### CreateCameras

Creates perspective cameras, each added at the end of the path of the given Camera Set, from the camera and target positions (with their heights) and optionally the view cone, roll angle, two-point perspective, sun (by angles or by date and time) and pen; the rest comes from the Camera tool defaults. Returns their element ids, which GetCameras lists. Delete them with DeleteElements.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.1. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateCameras

Parameters:

- `cameras` (array of object, required): The perspective cameras to create. Each is added at the end of the path of its Camera Set, in the order of this list. The values not given come from the Camera tool defaults.
  - `cameraSetElementId` (ElementId, required): The Camera Set (camera path) the camera is added to, as GetCameras or CreateCameraSets returns it.
  - `cameraPosition` (Coordinate3D, required): The position of the camera; z is its height.
  - `targetPosition` (Coordinate3D, required): The position of the target point the camera looks at; z is its height. Archicad works out the distance and the azimuth of the camera from the two positions.
  - `viewCone` (number): The view cone angle of the camera, in the units GetCameras returns it.
  - `rollAngle` (number): The roll angle of the camera, in the units GetCameras returns it.
  - `isTwoPointPersp` (boolean): True for a two-point perspective (vertical edges stay vertical).
  - `sun` (ProjectionSunSettings): The sun position of the camera's perspective, by angles or by date and time. Only the values given change; the others come from the Camera tool defaults.
  - `pen` (integer): The pen index of the camera's symbol on the floor plan.

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required): The element ids of the new cameras, in the order of the input, or an error for each one that could not be created. GetCameras lists them as cameraElementId.

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/CreateCameras.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/CreateCameras.py): Creates a Camera Set named "Viewpoints" with CreateCameraSets and adds two perspective cameras to its path with CreateCameras, the second one a two-point perspective with the sun given by date and time; then lists the cameras with GetCameras.

### ModifyCameras

Changes perspective cameras: the camera and target positions (with their heights), view cone, roll angle, two-point perspective, sun (by angles or by date and time) and pen. Values not given are kept; each camera keeps its element id, its Camera Set and its place in the path. View cone and roll angle are in the units GetCameras returns them.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.1. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ModifyCameras

Parameters:

- `cameras` (array of object, required): The perspective cameras to change, each with the values to change; the values not given are kept. A camera keeps its element id, its Camera Set and its place in the path.
  - `cameraElementId` (ElementId, required): The camera, as GetCameras or CreateCameras returns it.
  - `cameraPosition` (Coordinate3D): The new position of the camera; z is its height.
  - `targetPosition` (Coordinate3D): The new position of the target point the camera looks at; z is its height. Archicad works out the distance and the azimuth of the camera from the two positions.
  - `viewCone` (number): The view cone angle of the camera, in the units GetCameras returns it.
  - `rollAngle` (number): The roll angle of the camera, in the units GetCameras returns it.
  - `isTwoPointPersp` (boolean): True for a two-point perspective (vertical edges stay vertical).
  - `sun` (ProjectionSunSettings): The sun position of the camera's perspective, by angles or by date and time. Only the values given change; the others are kept.
  - `pen` (integer): The pen index of the camera's symbol on the floor plan.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required): One result for each camera of the input, in its order.

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/ModifyCameras.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/ModifyCameras.py): Creates a Camera Set with a camera using CreateCameraSets and CreateCameras, then moves the camera and its target, makes it a two-point perspective with a new sun and pen using ModifyCameras; the camera keeps its element id. Lists the cameras with GetCameras.

### Get3DDocumentSettings

Gets the settings of a 3D Document, given by its navigator item: the element and story filter, the 3D cut, the projection, the window and zoom, the uniform cut and uncut surface attributes, the source and the boundary contours, with the field names of API_DocumentFrom3DType.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#Get3DDocumentSettings

Parameters:

- `navigatorItemId` (NavigatorItemId, required): The navigator item of the 3D Document, from the Project Map or the View Map.

Returns:

- `settings` (object, required): The settings of the 3D Document, with the field names of API_DocumentFrom3DType.
  - `filterAndCutSettings` (object): Which elements and stories the 3D Document shows (API_3DFilterAndCutSettings). The marquee filter is not included.
  - `cutSetting` (object): The 3D cut of the 3D Document (API_3DCutPlanesInfo). The cut planes themselves are not included.
  - `cutaway3D` (boolean)
  - `projectionSetting` (object): The projection of the 3D Document (API_3DProjectionInfo). persp is present when isPersp is true, axono otherwise. Changing isPersp starts the new projection from zero, give persp or axono with it.
  - `floorPlanRotationOrigo` (Coordinate2D)
  - `window3DInfo` (object): API_3DWindowInfo of the 3D Document.
  - `hiddenLineType` (AttributeIdArrayItem): A line type. Missing when there is none.
  - `hiddenLineLen` (integer)
  - `effects3D` (integer)
  - `drawRect` (object)
  - `attributeOptions` (object): The uniform attributes of cut and uncut surfaces (API_UniformAttributeOptions). Pens and uniformLineType are indices; the enums fillCutSurfacesWith, uncutSurfaceFillType, hiddenEdgeVisibility and onCutPlaneVisibility are their integer values.
  - `currPlanConn` (string ("Online", "Offline", "Drawing"))
  - `intPlanConn` (string ("Online", "Offline", "Drawing"))
  - `materialFrom3D` (boolean)
  - `docSrc` (string ("DDD", "FloorPlan")): Whether the 3D Document comes from the 3D window or from the floor plan.
  - `skeletonOptions` (object): API_SkeletonOptions of a 3D Document made from the floor plan. viewSrc is the integer value of API_ViewSourceID.
  - `boundaryDisplay` (string ("UncutContours", "NoContours", "OverrideContours"))
  - `boundaryPen` (integer)
  - `boundaryLineType` (AttributeIdArrayItem): A line type. Missing when there is none.
  - `transparency` (boolean)

Needs at least one 3D Document.

Gets the grid and snap grid settings of the database of the current window, and which database that is. Each database has its own grid settings. Available from Archicad 27.

Parameters: none.


Grasshopper: `GetGridSettingsComponent`

Requires Archicad 27 or later.

### SetGridSettings

Changes the grid and snap grid settings of the database of the current window; only the given fields change. Returns the settings read back after the change. Available from Archicad 27.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SetGridSettings

Parameters:

- `settings` (object, required): The grid settings to change, in the form GetGridSettings returns. Only the given keys are changed; a color may give only some of its components.
  - `spaceMainX` (number): The horizontal spacing of the main grid, in meters.
  - `spaceMainY` (number): The vertical spacing of the main grid, in meters.
  - `nLineMainX` (integer): The number of main horizontal grid lines.
  - `nLineMainY` (integer): The number of main vertical grid lines.
  - `gridSwitch` (boolean): Whether the grid is visible.
  - `spaceAuxX` (number): The horizontal spacing of the auxiliary grid, in meters.
  - `spaceAuxY` (number): The vertical spacing of the auxiliary grid, in meters.
  - `nLineAuxX` (integer): The number of horizontal auxiliary grid lines.
  - `nLineAuxY` (integer): The number of vertical auxiliary grid lines.
  - `gridMode` (integer): 0: none, 1: grid, 2: snap.
  - `snapOffsX` (number): The horizontal offset of the snap grid, in meters.
  - `snapOffsY` (number): The vertical offset of the snap grid, in meters.
  - `snapStepX` (number): The horizontal spacing of the snap grid, in meters.
  - `snapStepY` (number): The vertical spacing of the snap grid, in meters.
  - `status` (integer): The status of the grid, as Archicad stores it.
  - `gridAngle` (number): The rotation angle of the grid.
  - `gridOffsX` (number): The X offset of the grid.
  - `gridOffsY` (number): The Y offset of the grid.
  - `gridOffsZ` (number): The Z offset of the grid.
  - `backColor` (object): A color with transparency, each component from 0 to 1. Archicad keeps 8 bits per component, so a value that is set is rounded to the nearest 1/255.
  - `gridColor` (object): A color with transparency, each component from 0 to 1. Archicad keeps 8 bits per component, so a value that is set is rounded to the nearest 1/255.

### ZoomToElements

Zooms the current window, 2D or 3D, to the given elements: selects them, zooms to the selection and restores the previous selection unless keepSelection is false. Fails when none of the elements could be selected, e.g. all of them are on another story or on a hidden layer.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ZoomToElements

Parameters:

- `elements` (Elements, required)
- `keepSelection` (boolean): Restore the selection the window had before the command (default). With false the given elements stay selected.

### CreateSections

Creates Section elements on the floor plan. A section looks to the left of its start to end direction, with its depth line that far on that side. GetDetailsOfElements reads the geometry of existing sections back. The floor plan must be the active window: creation fails while a Section or Elevation window is active.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 1.5.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateSections

Parameters:

- `sectionsData` (array of object, required)
  - `startCoordinate` (Coordinate2D, required)
  - `endCoordinate` (Coordinate2D, required)
  - `depth` (number): The distance of the depth line from the section line, on the left of the start to end direction, which is the direction the section looks in. Default is 1.
  - `name` (string)
  - `id` (string): The reference ID shown in the section marker and in the Project Map. A '/' splits it between the start and the end marker. Without it the section takes the ID of the Section tool defaults, or none with a favoriteName, as a Section favorite carries no ID.
  - `favoriteName` (string): Optional name of a Section favorite to base the new section on, marker included. Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them. The Section tool defaults are restored afterwards.
  - `floorIndex` (integer)
  - `details` (SectionElevationSettableDetails)

Returns:

- `elements` (ElementIdsOrErrors, required)

Grasshopper: `CreateSectionsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/CreateSections.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/CreateSections.py): Creates a 10 m long Section on the floor plan with CreateSections, then deletes it again. The section looks to the left of its start to end direction, here to the north.

### ModifySections

Changes the name and the reference ID of Section and Elevation elements, which the Project Map and the markers show, and moves their section line (startCoordinate, endCoordinate) and depth line (depth, only with the horizontal range Limited, which SetSectionsAndElevationsDetails sets). GetDetailsOfElements reads them back as name, idStr, startCoordinate, endCoordinate and depth.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ModifySections

Parameters:

- `sectionsWithDetails` (array of object, required)
  - `elementId` (ElementId, required): A Section or an Elevation.
  - `name` (string): The new name, shown in the Project Map.
  - `id` (string): The new reference ID, shown in the marker and in the Project Map. A '/' splits it between the start and the end marker.
  - `startCoordinate` (Coordinate2D): The new start point of the section line. Only a straight marker (a section line of 2 points, as CreateSections and CreateElevations make) can be moved. The depth line and the marked distant area line keep their distance from it.
  - `endCoordinate` (Coordinate2D): The new end point of the section line, as startCoordinate. The view looks to the side the depth line was on.
  - `depth` (number): The new distance of the depth line from the section line, on the side it is on. GetDetailsOfElements reads it back as depth. Only applies when the element's horizontalRange is Limited (SetSectionsAndElevationsDetails); refused otherwise.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `ModifySectionsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/ModifySections.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/ModifySections.py): Creates a Section with a Limited horizontal range (a depth only applies to one), changes its name and reference ID, moves its end point and its depth line with ModifySections and reads them back. Deletes the section at the end.

Deletes both folders at the end.

### RenameNavigatorItem

Renames a navigator item or changes its ID. Renaming the Layout Book item of a placed Drawing also sets the custom name of the Drawing. newId sets the custom layout number of a layout and the custom ID of any other item. For a Project Map section, elevation, detail or worksheet the name and ID of the element behind the viewpoint are changed, for an interior elevation those of the segment the item stands for; the change is undone when the item does not show the new name. The name and ID of other Project Map items (stories, schedules, ...) cannot be changed. Fails when Archicad refuses the change or does not apply the new name or ID. With customName false the item drops its custom name and follows its Project Map source again.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 1.1.7. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#RenameNavigatorItem

Parameters:

- `navigatorItemId` (NavigatorItemId, required)
- `newName` (string): The new name of the item. On the Layout Book item of a placed Drawing it is also set as the custom name of the Drawing (nameType CustomName).
- `newId` (string): The new ID of the item. On a layout it is the custom layout number (customLayoutNumbering is switched on); on a Project Map section, elevation, interior elevation, detail or worksheet it is the reference ID of the element behind the item; on any other item it is the custom ID of the navigator item (customUiId becomes true).
- `customName` (boolean): Set to false to drop the custom name of the item, so that it follows the name of its Project Map source again. Cannot be combined with newName.


Grasshopper: `RenameNavigatorItem`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/RenameNavigatorItem.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/RenameNavigatorItem.py): Creates a View Map folder and renames it with RenameNavigatorItem. Deletes the folder at the end.

### DeleteNavigatorItems

Deletes navigator items from the navigator tree: views and folders of the View Map, layouts and master layouts of the Layout Book, and independent worksheets and details of the Project Map. Layout subsets, View Map folders that are not empty, the other Project Map items and marker-linked worksheets and details cannot be deleted; the failed execution result says which case applies. An item that Archicad refuses to delete (in a Teamwork project: it is not reserved or the user has no right to delete it) is reported as a failed execution result. dryRun reports the result of the checks made before deleting (item not found, layout subset, View Map folder that is not empty) without deleting anything.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 1.1.7. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#DeleteNavigatorItems

Parameters:

- `navigatorItemIds` (NavigatorItemIds, required)
- `dryRun` (boolean): If true, nothing is deleted: each execution result says what the deletion would do for that item, from the checks made before deleting (corrupt id, item not found, layout subset, View Map folder that is not empty). Archicad can still refuse an item that passes them: a Project Map item other than an independent worksheet, detail or viewpoint created by the Tapir Add-On, a marker-linked worksheet or detail, or in a Teamwork project an item that is not reserved. Default is false.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `DeleteNavigatorItem`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/DeleteNavigatorItems.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/DeleteNavigatorItems.py): Creates an independent Worksheet and deletes it from the Project Map with DeleteNavigatorItems, first as a dry run that deletes nothing.

### GetNavigatorItemTree

Returns the full navigator item tree for the specified map. With includeChildCount true every item also reports the number of its direct children.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 1.1.7. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetNavigatorItemTree

Parameters:

- `navigatorMapId` (string ("PublicViewMap", "ProjectMap", "LayoutBook", "PublisherSets"), required): The navigator map to retrieve.
- `publisherSetName` (string): The name of the publisher set to retrieve. Used only when navigatorMapId is PublisherSets. Without it the first publisher set is returned.
- `includeChildCount` (boolean): Set to true to add childCount, the number of direct children Archicad reports, to every item. Defaults to false.

Grasshopper: `GetNavigatorItemTreeComponent`

The other maps are ProjectMap, PublicViewMap and PublisherSets (with publisherSetName).

### GetSchedules

Returns the Interactive Schedules of the Project Map: navigator item id, name, ID and the folders they are in. Archicad's API does not give the rows of a schedule nor export it; to export one, put it in a publisher set with a spreadsheet format in Archicad and run PublishPublisherSet.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetSchedules

  - `uiId` (string, required): The ID of the schedule, shown before its name in the navigator.
  - `folderPath` (array of string, required): The names of the Project Map items the schedule is in, from the top down, without the project itself (e.g. Schedules, Element). Archicad's API does not say whether a schedule lists elements, components or surfaces; the default Project Map shows it by these folders.

Each line shows the folders the schedule is in, its ID and its name.

### CreateAddOnViewpoints

Creates add-on viewpoint roots, groups and leaf nodes in the Project Map, with their ID, name, view settings flags (leaf nodes only) and attached data (base64 encoded). A group or a leaf node is created in the given parent root or group. Returns the identifier of each new item, or an error for an item that could not be created. Roots and groups can't be created in a Teamwork project. Available from Archicad 27.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateAddOnViewpoints

Parameters:

- `viewpoints` (array of object, required): The add-on viewpoint items to create. The identifier of a new root or group is only known from the response, so create the parents in an earlier call.
  - `itemType` (AddOnViewpointType, required)
  - `parentViewpointId` (object): The root or group to create the item in. Required for a group or a leaf node, ignored for a root.
  - `displayId` (string): The ID shown for the item in the Project Map.
  - `displayName` (string): The name shown for the item in the Project Map.
  - `viewSettingsFlags` (integer): The view settings flags of a leaf node, as Archicad stores them (a bit field). Ignored for a root or a group.
  - `data` (string): Data to attach to the item, base64 encoded.

Returns:

- `viewpoints` (array of object or ErrorItem, required): The identifier of each created item, in the order of the input, or an error for an item that could not be created.

Grasshopper: `CreateAddOnViewpointsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/CreateAddOnViewpoints.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/CreateAddOnViewpoints.py): Creates an add-on viewpoint root with a leaf node in it, using CreateAddOnViewpoints. The new items stay in the Project Map. Roots can't be created in a Teamwork project. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

Changes the ID, name, view settings flags or attached data (base64 encoded) of the given add-on viewpoint items; only the given fields are changed. Roots and groups can't be changed in a Teamwork project. Available from Archicad 27.

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 1.8.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ChangeAddOnViewpoints

Needs an add-on viewpoint. Roots can't be changed in a Teamwork project. Requires Archicad 27 or later.

### ReorderNavigatorItems

Reorders the children of a navigator item to match the given order. Works around MoveNavigatorItem being unable to reposition an item within its current parent, by bouncing it through a sibling folder, or through the parent's own parent when no sibling can host it (for example a folder with only views and clone folders).

Group: Navigator Commands. Added in Tapir 2.0.0. Docs: https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ReorderNavigatorItems

Parameters:

- `parentNavigatorItemId` (NavigatorItemId, required): The folder whose children should be reordered.
- `orderedNavigatorItemIds` (array of NavigatorItemIdArrayItem, required): The complete, desired order of every child of parentNavigatorItemId. Every current child must be listed.

Returns:

- `executionResults` (ExecutionResults, required)

Grasshopper: `ReorderNavigatorItemsComponent`

Example: [archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/ReorderNavigatorItems.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Navigator/ReorderNavigatorItems.py): Creates a View Map folder with two subfolders and swaps their order with ReorderNavigatorItems. Deletes the folders at the end.

## Shared schema definitions

Types that parameters and results refer to by name.

### Elements

array of ElementIdArrayItem: A list of elements.

### ElementIdArrayItem

object
- `elementId` (ElementId, required)

### ElementIdOrError

ElementIdArrayItem or ErrorItem: An element identifier or an error.

### ElementIdsOrErrors

array of ElementIdOrError: A list of element identifiers or errors.

### ElementId

object: The identifier of an element.
- `guid` (Guid, required)

### AttributeIdArrayItem

object
- `attributeId` (AttributeId, required)

### AttributeId

object: The identifier of an attribute.
- `guid` (Guid, required)

### GuidId

object: Identifier.
- `guid` (Guid, required)

### ModelViewOptionId

object: The identifier of the model view option combination.
- `guid` (Guid, required)

### ViewOptions

object: The model view options and the on-screen view options, every field by its API_ViewOptions name. Values are the numeric API constants; attribute indices are plain integers.
- `modelViewOptions` (object, required): Fields of API_ModelViewOptions, with the curtainWall, stair and railing parts as nested objects.
  - `railing` (RailingModelViewOptions)
- `onScreenViewOptions` (object, required): Fields of API_OnScreenViewOptions.

### ViewOptionsUpdate

object: The fields to change, named as in the response of GetViewOptions. Fields not given keep their current value. Without an index, the window then uses Custom model view options (index 0), also when only on-screen view options are given. To keep the combination, give its index as well. The options are read back, and a given field Archicad did not keep fails the call with the value it kept.
- `modelViewOptions` (object)
  - `railing` (RailingModelViewOptions): The railing options to change; the ones left out keep their value. Archicad 29 does not keep the railing2DDisplayComp* fields, which SetViewOptions then reports.
- `onScreenViewOptions` (object)

### RailingModelViewOptions

object: The railing options of the model view options (API_RailingModelViewOptions; Model View Options > Railing Options), every field by its API name: the railing components shown in the floor plan and the schematic 3D display. GetViewOptions and GetModelViewOptionDetails return all of them; SetViewOptions takes any of them and reads them back. Archicad 29 does not keep the railing2DDisplayComp* fields changed through ACAPI_Navigator_ChangeViewOptions, so SetViewOptions reports such a change as not kept.
- `railing3DDetailLevel` (integer): The detail level of railings in the 3D display, the numeric API constant.
- `railing2DDisplayCompPosts` (boolean): Whether the posts are shown in the floor plan.
- `railing2DDisplayCompTopRail` (boolean): Whether the top rails are shown in the floor plan.
- `railing2DDisplayCompHandrails` (boolean): Whether the handrails are shown in the floor plan.
- `railing2DDisplayCompRails` (boolean): Whether the rails are shown in the floor plan.
- `railing2DDisplayCompInnerPosts` (boolean): Whether the inner posts are shown in the floor plan.
- `railing2DDisplayCompBalusters` (boolean): Whether the balusters are shown in the floor plan.
- `railing2DDisplayCompPanels` (boolean): Whether the panels are shown in the floor plan.
- `railingSchemeSurfaceIndex` (integer): The index of the surface used by the schematic 3D display.
- `railingSchemeCutLineIndex` (integer): The index of the line type of the cut lines of the schematic 3D display.
- `railingSchemeCutLinePenIndex` (integer): The pen of the cut lines of the schematic 3D display.
- `railingSchemeUncutLineIndex` (integer): The index of the line type of the uncut lines of the schematic 3D display.
- `railingSchemeUncutLinePenIndex` (integer): The pen of the uncut lines of the schematic 3D display.

### RenovationFilterDetails

object
- `renovationFilterId` (GuidId, required): Identifier of the renovation filter. The same identifier is the renovationFilterGuid of GetViewSettings and SetViewSettings.
- `name` (string, required): Name of the renovation filter.

### AddOnViewpointDetails

object
- `viewpointId` (object, required): The identifier of the add-on viewpoint item.
  - `guid` (Guid, required)
- `parentViewpointId` (object): The identifier of the root or group the item is in. Missing when Archicad reports no parent, as for a root.
  - `guid` (Guid, required)
- `itemType` (string ("Root", "Group", "Leaf", "Undefined"), required): Whether the item is a root, a group or a leaf node.
- `displayId` (string, required): The ID shown for the item in the Project Map.
- `displayName` (string, required): The name shown for the item in the Project Map.
- `viewSettingsFlags` (integer, required): The view settings flags of the item, as Archicad stores them (a bit field).
- `data` (string, required): The data the add-on attached to the item, base64 encoded. Empty when there is none.

### AddOnViewpointType

string ("Root", "Group", "Leaf"): Whether to create a root, a group or a leaf node. Roots and groups can't be created in a Teamwork project.

### AddOnViewpointModificationData

object
- `viewpointId` (object, required): The identifier of the add-on viewpoint item to change.
  - `guid` (Guid, required)
- `displayId` (string): The ID shown for the item in the Project Map.
- `displayName` (string): The name shown for the item in the Project Map.
- `viewSettingsFlags` (integer): The view settings flags of the item, as Archicad stores them (a bit field).
- `data` (string): Data to attach to the item, base64 encoded. It replaces the attached data; an empty string removes it.

### Guid

string: A Globally Unique Identifier (or Universally Unique Identifier) in its string representation as defined in RFC 4122.

### PolyArc

object: Representation of an arc segment of a two dimensional polygon/polyline.
- `begIndex` (integer, required): Node index of one end point of the arc.
- `endIndex` (integer, required): Node index of the other end point of the arc.
- `arcAngle` (number, required): Angle of the arc; it is positive, if the arc is on the right-hand side of the straight segment.

### Coordinate2D

object: 2D coordinate.
- `x` (number, required): X value of the coordinate.
- `y` (number, required): Y value of the coordinate.

### Coordinate3D

object: 3D coordinate.
- `x` (number, required): X value of the coordinate.
- `y` (number, required): Y value of the coordinate.
- `z` (number, required): Z value of the coordinate.

### AxonometryProjectionType

string ("YZ", "XZ", "XY", "Frontal", "Monometric", "Isometric", "Dimetric", "Bottom", "FrontalBottom", "MonometricBottom", "IsometricBottom", "DimetricBottom", ...): The projection type of an axonometric 3D projection, the projMod of the Archicad API. Archicad works out the transformation matrix of every type but Custom from the type and the azimuth. XY is the top view and Bottom the view from below. YZ and XZ are both the side view (an elevation), looking from the azimuth. Frontal, Monometric, Isometric and Dimetric are the predefined axonometries, and FrontalBottom, MonometricBottom, IsometricBottom and DimetricBottom the same seen from below; an Isometric at azimuth 270 is the isometric from the south-east (X axis at -30 degrees, Y at 30, Z at 90). Custom keeps the transformation matrix as given. Parallel cannot be set: Archicad makes it Custom.

### PerspectiveProjectionParameters

object: The parameters of a perspective projection of the 3D window.
- `cameraPosition` (Coordinate3D, required): The position of the camera.
- `targetPosition` (Coordinate3D, required): The position of the target point the camera looks at.
- `distance` (number, required): The distance between the camera and the target.
- `azimuth` (number, required): The azimuth of the camera in degrees: the direction from the target to the camera, counterclockwise from the X axis. Archicad works it out from the camera and target positions, so a set value is replaced by that.
- `viewCone` (number, required): The view cone angle of the camera in degrees.
- `rollAngle` (number, required): The roll angle of the camera.
- `isTwoPointPersp` (boolean, required): True for a two-point perspective (vertical edges stay vertical).
- `sun` (ProjectionSunSettings): The sun position of the perspective. Get3DProjectionSettings always returns it; Set3DProjectionSettings changes only the values given and keeps the current sun when it is missing.

### ProjectionSunSettings

object: The sun position of a 3D projection, the Sun Position of the 3D Projection Settings dialog (API_SunAngleSettings). Each perspective and axonometry has its own, independent of the project's date and time (SetSunSettings). The 3D shading and shadows of the projection come from it.
- `sunPositionOption` (string ("Angles", "DateAndTime")): Angles: the sun is at sunAzimuth and sunAltitude. DateAndTime: Archicad calculates the sun from the project location and the date and time given here.
- `sunAzimuth` (number): The azimuth of the sun, used when sunPositionOption is Angles. In the same units Get3DProjectionSettings returns it.
- `sunAltitude` (number): The altitude of the sun, used when sunPositionOption is Angles. In the same units Get3DProjectionSettings returns it.
- `year` (integer): Used when sunPositionOption is DateAndTime. 0 when no date is set.
- `month` (integer): Used when sunPositionOption is DateAndTime. 0 when no date is set.
- `day` (integer): Used when sunPositionOption is DateAndTime. 0 when no date is set.
- `hour` (integer)
- `minute` (integer)
- `second` (integer)
- `summerTime` (boolean): True when the time is daylight saving time.

### ColorRGB

object: RGB color.
- `red` (number, required): Red value between 0.0 and 1.0
- `green` (number, required): Green value between 0.0 and 1.0
- `blue` (number, required): Blue value between 0.0 and 1.0

### Error

object: The details of an error.
- `code` (integer, required): The code of the error.
- `message` (string, required): The error message.

### ErrorItem

object
- `error` (Error, required)

### SuccessfulExecutionResult

object: The result of a successful execution.
- `success` (boolean (true), required)

### FailedExecutionResult

object: The result of a failed execution.
- `success` (boolean (false), required)
- `error` (Error, required)

### ExecutionResult

SuccessfulExecutionResult or FailedExecutionResult: The result of the execution.

### ExecutionResults

array of ExecutionResult: A list of execution results.

### ElementType

string ("Wall", "Column", "Beam", "Window", "Door", "Object", "Lamp", "Slab", "Roof", "Mesh", "Dimension", "RadialDimension", ...): The type of an element.

### DrawingNameType

string ("ViewOrSourceFileName", "ViewIdAndName", "CustomName"): How the drawing's title name is assembled (Identification tabpage of the Drawing Settings dialog).

### DrawingAnchorPoint

string ("TopLeft", "TopCenter", "TopRight", "MiddleLeft", "Center", "MiddleRight", "BottomLeft", "BottomCenter", "BottomRight"): The node of the drawing's bounding box the drawing is placed by (API_DrawingType::anchorPoint). Used only when useOwnOriginAsAnchor is false.

### NavigatorItemType

string ("UndefinedItem", "ProjectItem", "StoryItem", "SectionItem", "DetailDrawingItem", "PerspectiveItem", "AxonometryItem", "ListItem", "ScheduleItem", "TocItem", "CameraItem", "CameraSetItem", ...): The type of the navigator item.

### InteriorElevationData

object
- `nodeCoordinates` (array of Coordinate2D, required): The corner points of the connected segment chain. Each consecutive pair of points becomes one segment, so a room with four walls needs five points to be closed, or four to be left open.
- `depth` (number): How far each segment looks. Applied to every segment. Defaults to 1.0.
- `name` (string): Name of the interior elevation. Each segment is named after it.
- `id` (string): ID string of the interior elevation.
- `floorIndex` (integer): The story to place the interior elevation on. Defaults to the current story. Archicad places an interior elevation on the active story, so for another story that story is activated while the interior elevation is created, and the previously active one is put back afterwards.

### StoredGDLParameter

object: A GDL parameter as it is stored with a marker or a Favorite, read without a parameter interface (so without isLocked and possibleValues).
- `name` (string, required): The name of the parameter.
- `displayName` (string, required): The display name of the parameter.
- `index` (integer, required): The index of the parameter.
- `type` (string, required): The type of the parameter.
- `dimension1` (integer): The 1st dimension of array (in case of array value).
- `dimension2` (integer): The 2nd dimension of array (in case of array value).
- `value` (any): The value of the parameter.
- `valueDescription` (string): The value description for numeric parameter.
- `itemDescriptions` (array of string): Per-item text labels for an array-type parameter, one per array element in dim1xdim2 order. Only present when the library part defines them.
- `flags` (array of string ("Hidden", "HiddenFromScript", "Disabled", "Child", "Unique", "Fixed", "BoldName", "Open"), required): The flags of the parameter.

### NavigatorItemIds

array of NavigatorItemIdArrayItem: A list of navigator item identifiers.

### NavigatorItemIdOrError

NavigatorItemIdArrayItem or ErrorItem: A propertyId or an error.

### NavigatorItemIdArrayItem

object
- `navigatorItemId` (NavigatorItemId, required)

### NavigatorItemId

object: The identifier of a navigator item.
- `guid` (Guid, required)

### NavigatorItem

object: A navigator item and the subtree below it.
- `navigatorItemId` (NavigatorItemId, required)
- `type` (NavigatorItemType, required)
- `name` (string, required): The name of the navigator item.
- `autoTextedName` (string): The name of the navigator item as it was given, with its autotext tokens (e.g. <PROJECTNUMBER>_<SourceID>_<SourceItemName>), while name holds it with the tokens resolved. Only present when the two differ, that is when the name contains autotext.
- `prefix` (string, required): The floor number for story items, an empty string for every other item type.
- `uiId` (string, required): The identifier shown next to the name on the navigator.
- `customUiId` (boolean, required): True when the identifier was typed by hand instead of being inherited from the Project Map source - the View Settings ID "Custom" radio button.
- `customName` (boolean, required): True when the name was typed by hand instead of being inherited from the Project Map source - the View Settings name "Custom" radio button.
- `isIndependent` (boolean, required): True when the item is independent, that is when its link to the Project Map is broken.
- `sourceNavigatorItemId` (NavigatorItemId): The identifier of the navigator item this one was created from: the Project Map item behind a view, or the source view behind a placed Drawing's Layout Book entry. Missing when the item has no such source; Project Map items never do.
- `childCount` (integer): The number of direct children Archicad reports for the item. Only present when GetNavigatorItemTree is called with includeChildCount true.
- `children` (array of NavigatorItemArrayItem): The children of the navigator item. Missing when the item has no children.
